ITQAN:v3p103/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r16.claim: Likewise, الإنسان in 70:19 is collective, as the later exception for those who pray shows.
ITQAN:v3p103/r16.anchor: ﴿ إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا ﴾ بدليل ﴿ إلا المصلين ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p123/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p123/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p123/r4.claim: Humankind was created intensely anxious: quick to despair when harm such as poverty or illness arrives, and quick to withhold when benefit arrives; Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the person is content when possessing and resentful when losing.
BURSEVI:v10p123/r4.anchor: سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه بحيث لا يستمسك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.claim: People generally become frustrated and complain when God punishes them even a little for their deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.anchor: people generally become frustrated and start complaining if the Almighty punishes them a little

QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.claim: The ego is inherently a source of evil and impurity; attachment to its dark nature produces cowardice and greed, shown by despair under harm and withholding good.
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.anchor: النفس بطبعها معدن الشر ومأوى الرجس لكونها من عالم الظلمات

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r1.claim: Qatada glosses halu'a as fretful or easily distressed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ هلوعا ﴾ قال جزوعا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r2.claim: Hasan instead glosses it as greedy.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p317#3/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال الحسن هو الشره

SULAMI:v2p350#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r1.claim: The restless human continually shifts with desires and follows caprice.
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r1.anchor: قال سهل : متقلب في حركات الشهوات واتباع الهوى

SULAMI:v2p350#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r2.claim: The restless person is content when possessing something and resentful when it is lost.
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r2.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا القاسم البزاز يقول : سمعت ابن عطاء قال الهلوع الذي عند الموجود يرضى

SULAMI:v2p350#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r3.claim: The restless person is ignorant and greedy, satisfied with little worldly gain yet angered by losing a like amount.
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : جهولا ، وقال أيضا طموعا يرضيه القليل من الدنيا ويسخطه مثلها

SULAMI:v2p350#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الوراق
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r4.claim: The restless person curses in affliction and supplicates when tested.
SULAMI:v2p350#5/r4.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الوراق : نساء عند النقمة ودعاء عند المحنة

TUSTARI:70:19/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:70:19/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:70:19/r1.claim: The human being’s restlessness means fluctuating with the movements of desire and following appetite.
TUSTARI:70:19/r1.anchor: يعني متقلبا في حركات الشهوات واتباع الهوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.claim: Asked by Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir what hala' means, he says the following verses define it: distress makes a person intensely anxious and prosperity makes him withhold.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.anchor: وقال ثعلب: قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر: ما الهلع؟ فقلت: قد فسره الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.claim: Human anxiety and withholding are so entrenched that humanity is described as created bearing them, as in 21:37; al-khayr here means wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.anchor: ولما كان شدة الجزع والمنع متمكنة في الإنسان، جعل كأنه خلق محمولا عليهما كقوله:

FARRA:v3p185/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p185/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p185/r3.claim: Haluʿ means irritable and impatient; the next verses define it as despairing in harm and withholding in good, from the root pattern of jazaʿ.
FARRA:v3p185/r3.anchor: والهلوع: الضجور وصفته كما قال الله: «إذا مسه الشر جزوعا»

MAJAZ:v2p270/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p270/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p270/r1.claim: Halūʿ means one who does not endure patiently, as God explains it in the next verses.
MAJAZ:v2p270/r1.anchor: «إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا» (19) قد فسرها الله: لا يصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.claim: Haluʿ describes swift panic at harm and swift withholding when good comes, from a word for a fast-moving she-camel.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.anchor: الهلع سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه وسرعة المنع عند مس الخير من قولهم ناقة هلوع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that when Ibn Abbas was asked about haluʿ, he answered by reciting the next verse's description.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وغيرهما عن عكرمة قال سئل ابن عباس عن الهلوع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.claim: Al-Hasan likewise answered a question about the term by reciting the verse; Thaʿlab says the verse itself is the clearest possible explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن الحسن أنه سئل عن ذلك أيضا فقرأ الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.claim: The emphatic sentence explains the reason for the preceding statement; الإنسان may mean humanity generally or unbelievers specifically.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.anchor: والجملة المؤكدة في موضع التعليل لما قبلها والإنسان الجنس أو الكافر قولان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Tusti says the verse concerns Abu Jahl, though a specific example does not preclude a generic meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.anchor: أن الآية في أبي جهل بن هشام ولا يأبى ذاك إرادة الجنس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reports from Ibn Abbas that هَلُوع means greedy for what is unlawful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r4.anchor: روى السدي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس [قال] (4) "الهلوع" الحريص على ما لا يحل له.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r5.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr glosses هَلُوع as miserly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan gloss هَلُوع as stingy.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r9.claim: Muqatil says the word means narrow-hearted; lexically, it combines intense greed with little patience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ضيق القلب. والهلع: شدة الحرص وقلة الصبر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.claim: God created people to love pleasure and flee pain, then commanded them to give what they love and patiently bear what they dislike.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: خلق الله الإنسان يحب ما يسره ويهرب مما يكره، ثم تعبده بإنفاق ما يحب

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r2.claim: هَلوع means intensely greedy and poorly patient.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r2.anchor: { إن الإنسن خلق هلوعا } شديد الحرص قليل الصبر

NAHHAS:v5p29/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p29/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p29/r19.claim: Khuliqa is inna's predicate and halūʿan a circumstantial accusative; lexicographers describe despair when poor and withholding obligatory rights when wealthy.
NAHHAS:v5p29/r19.anchor: خلق في موضع خبر إن ونصبت ( هلوعا ) على الحال المقدرة والهلوع فيما حكاه أهل اللغة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r4.claim: Humanity is naturally self-absorbed, admiring itself and forgetting its Lord and sins; it was created with an intense mix of distress, greed, impatience, and miserliness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r4.anchor: الإنسان مقهور مع جبلته إلا من حفظه الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains haluʿ as being greedy for what is unlawful; another report from him says the following two clauses explain the word.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r5.anchor: أنه الحريص على ما لا يحل له

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas calls haluʿ impatient and easily distressed, says it was revealed about Abu Jahl, and cites Bashr ibn Abi Hazim's poetry for the word's Arabic usage.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses haluʿ as miserly and easily distressed.
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r5.claim: Qatada glosses haluʿ as given to anguish.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses haluʿ as greedy.
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r7.speaker: حصين بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r7.claim: Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman glosses haluʿ as avid or grasping.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak describes haluʿ as someone never satisfied with gathering wealth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.claim: Verses 19–21 interrupt the discussion between the one who hoards and the exception for worshippers; they summarize the human trait that drives greed and retention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.anchor: معترضة بين { من أدبر وتولى وجمع فأوعى } ( المعارج : 17 18 ) وبين الاستثناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.claim: This is a rebuke, not an excuse or justification for hoarding; fear of losing what benefits them explains the trait but does not absolve it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.anchor: وهذا تذييل لوم وليس في مساقه عذر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r5.claim: The emphatic إن draws attention to the startling human trait and warns against it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r5.anchor: وموقع حرف التوكيد ما تتضمنه الجملة من التعجيب من هذه الخصلة البشرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r7.claim: الإنسان denotes humanity as a species, not one individual, as in verses about human arrogance and haste.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r7.anchor: فالمراد بالإنسان : جنس الإنسان لا فرد معين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r8.claim: هلوع is an intensive adjective describing a strong tendency to panic and withhold.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r8.anchor: وهلوع : فعول مثال مبالغة للاتصاف بالهلع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r9.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى (ثعلب)
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r9.claim: Al-Kashshaf recounts Thalab's definition to Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir: the verse itself defines the person who intensely despairs at harm and keeps good from others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r9.anchor: وعن أحمد بن يحيى ( هو ثعلب ) قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r10.claim: Ibn Ashur says Thalab's definition is loose and imprecise: if the two following clauses define one compound trait, their distinct meanings would need to entail each other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r10.anchor: فسارت كلمة ثعلب مسيرا أقنع كثيرا من اللغويين عن زيادة الضبط لمعنى الهلع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r11.claim: Many linguists equate halʿ with distress, but distress is an effect of halʿ rather than the trait itself; the distinction is tested by the cited verse of Amr ibn Ma'dikarib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r11.anchor: وكثيرا من أيمة اللغة فسر الهلع بالجزع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r1.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r1.claim: His line distinguishes halʿ from jazaʿ by denying both separately; al-Marzūqī's attempt to read them as mild and severe grief does not resolve the difficulty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r1.anchor: ما إن جزعت ولا هلعت ولا يرد بكاي زندا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r2.claim: He defines halʿ as weak self-restraint when facing or anticipating what saddens or pleases a person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r2.anchor: أن الهلع قلة إمساك النفس عند اعتراء ما يحزنها أو ما يسرها أو عند توقع ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r3.claim: Other lexical glosses include greed, irritation, miserliness, hunger, or cowardice; these are effects of the broader trait he defines.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r3.anchor: وقد فسر بعض أهل اللغة الهلع بالشره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r4.claim: Being created halūʿ means this tendency is latent in human nature and appears when people first perceive benefit or harm; it does not preclude contrary states or moral training.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r4.anchor: أن الهلع طبيعة كامنة فيه مع خلقه تظهر عند ابتداء شعوره بالنافع والمضار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r5.claim: Because the trait follows the condemnation of hoarding, the wording implies people can restrain it by considering consequences and disciplining their weaknesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r5.anchor: فقد أشعر بأن الإنسان يستطيع أن يكف عن هلعه إذا تدبر في العواقب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r6.claim: The verse means human cognition tends toward halʿ; saying it is created in people highlights how strongly the tendency can dominate them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p167/r6.anchor: والمعنى : أن من مقتضى تركيب الإدراك البشري أن يحدث فيه الهلع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r1.claim: Attributing defects to human creation assigns responsibility: people fail to train their good disposition, indulge their impulses, and neglect the advice of revelation and wise people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r1.anchor: فالمقصود من ذلك : إلقاء تبعة ذلك عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r2.claim: Attributing good to God recalls His gift of the faculty that seeks good and His guidance and awakening to truth, as 4:78–79 explains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r2.anchor: وإذا أسند ما يأتيه الإنسان من الخير إلى الله تعالى فالمقصود : التنبيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r3.claim: He says the Mu'tazilites went astray in this theological question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r3.anchor: وفي هذا المجال زلت أفهام المعتزلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r4.claim: When خلق الإنسان describes a nonmaterial trait, it can mean a human disposition quickly attaches to feelings and actions, warning against its harm, as in the description of haste.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r4.anchor: واعلم أن كلمة ( خلق الإنسان ) إذا تعلق بها ما ليس من المواد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r5.claim: The creation wording can also soften blame by noting human weakness, or distinguish original good creation from later deterioration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r5.anchor: وقد ترد للعذر والرفق نحو قوله : { يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r6.claim: خلق from a trait can be metaphorical for persistent association; Urwa ibn Udhayna's poem argues that love remains because both lovers were created disposed to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p169/r6.anchor: ففعل الخلق من كذا مستعار لكثرة الملابسة . قال عروة بن أذينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.claim: The essence reading is like “man is better than woman,” or Imru al-Qays's line that war is initially young, and resembles the use in al-Maʿarij.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.anchor: ومنه التعريف الواقع في قوله تعالى : { إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r16.claim: الإنسان is a generic noun, but the intended referent here is unbelievers because the warning applies especially and forcefully to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r16.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إن الإنسان عموم لاسم الجنس، لكن الإشارة هنا إلى الكفار، لأن الأمر فيهم وكيد كثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.claim: هلع is anxious agitation that overtakes a person amid fears and desires; the author begins to compare it with a Prophetic saying.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.anchor: والهلع جزع واضطراب يعتري الإنسان عند المخاوف وعند المطامع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r1.claim: The human described as anxious is Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل عنى به أمية بن خلف الجمحي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو عبيدة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r2.claim: One interpretation is the set of traits described in the following verses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r2.anchor: أنه الموصوف بما يلي هذه الآية رواه عطية عن ابن عباس وبه قال أبو عبيدة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r3.claim: Another interpretation is someone greedy for what is not lawful for him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r3.anchor: أنه الحريص على ما لا يحل له رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r7.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة ومقاتل والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r7.anchor: الضجور قاله عكرمه وقتادة ومقاتل والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363/r8.claim: Halūʿ means intensely prone to distress.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r1.claim: Humans are innately impatient: when harmed they panic, are overwhelmed by fear, and despair of future good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r1.anchor: إذا أصابه الضر فزع وجزع وانخلع قلبه من شدة الرعب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.claim: The Prophet called anxious greed and paralyzing cowardice the worst traits in a man; Abu Dawud gives the same report through this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "شر ما في رجل شح هالع، وجبن خالع".

JISHUMI:v10p7081/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the plural amānāt with no alif after the nūn; the remaining readers have the plural with alif.
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: لأمانتهم بغير ألف بعد النون على واحدة

JISHUMI:v10p7081/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r5.claim: Haluʿ is swift and agitated; Abu Muslim gives the example of a fast, light she-camel. Another explanation is extreme greed coupled with the worst anxiety.
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r5.anchor: الهلوع: العجول الضجور، وناقة هلواع: إذا كانت سريعة خفيفة، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7081/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r9.claim: Haluʿan is accusative as a circumstantial expression.
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r9.anchor: هلوعا نصب على الحال، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7081/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r11.claim: Haluʿ means greedy and impatient: the human is created desirous and hastens to satisfy desire with little patience, so must be taught patience and restraint; desire is necessary for moral responsibility.
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r11.anchor: قيل: الهلوع الحريص الضجور، يعني خلق مشتهيا فهو يستبق إلى شهواته، ويقل صبره عنها

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains haluʿ by the following traits: when afflicted by harm, one is anxious, and when given good, one withholds it.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.anchor: وإذا مسه الخير منوعا (21)، عن عطية عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says haluʿ means stingy.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r2.anchor: وقيل: شحيحا، عن سعيد بن جبير

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r3.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r3.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd explain it as being highly anxious.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r3.anchor: وقيل: جزوعا، عن قتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r4.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say it means greedy and voracious.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r4.anchor: وقيل: حريصا شرها، عن مجاهد، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r5.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r5.claim: Muqatil interprets haluʿ as narrowness of heart.

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r6.claim: Al-Asamm says God created people loving what pleases them and hating what hurts them, then commands them to give what they love and endure what they dislike.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r6.anchor: وقيل: خلقه الله تعالى يحب ما يسره ويرضيه ويكره ما يدهيه، ثم تعبده بإنفاق ما يحب

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة وثعلب
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.claim: They say the person fails to give thanks when blessed and fails to be patient when afflicted.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، وثعلب، وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.speaker: سهل
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.claim: Sahl explains the traits as anxiety when poor and stinginess when prosperous.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.anchor: وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع، عن سهل

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r10.claim: The description may refer specifically to disbelievers or to all people; alternatively, humans are created weak in bearing these traits, not with the traits fully formed from infancy, but desirous, needy, and weak, which leads to impatience and withholding.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r10.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالكفار خاصة، وقيل: الخلق عامة، وقيل: خلق ضعيفا عن الصبر على الهلع والجزع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r1.claim: Here الإنسان means people generally, which is why worshippers are excepted from the description of being halūʿ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r1.anchor: أريد بالإنسان الناس ؛ فلذلك استثنى منه إلا المصلين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r2.claim: Halūʿ describes quick despair when harmed and quick withholding when good arrives; its root suggests a fast-moving she-camel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r2.anchor: والهلع : سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه وسرعة المنع عند مس الخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r3.claim: Asked by Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Tahir what halūʿ means, Ahmad ibn Yahya answered that God's own explanation is the clearest: despair in hardship and withholding in prosperity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r3.anchor: وعن أحمد بن يحيى ، قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر : ما الهلع ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r4.claim: Good and evil may mean wealth and poverty, or health and sickness: a healthy rich person withholds charity, while illness makes him complain and give instructions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r4.anchor: والخير : المال والغنى ؛ والشر : الفقر . أو الصحة والمرض : إذا صح الغني منع المعروف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r5.claim: People are so habituated to despair and withholding that these seem innate, as in ‘the human was created hasty’; yet the description is learned, since infants lack it and believers discipline themselves against it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r5.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { خلق الإنسان من عجل } ( الأنبياء : 37 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r6.claim: The Prophet calls a miserly, despairing disposition and a fear that strips one of courage among the worst gifts given to Adam's son.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r6.anchor: شر ما أعطى ابن آدم شح هالع وجبن خالع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r7.claim: Being constant in prayer means performing it regularly without neglect or distraction; guarding prayer means perfecting ablution, timing, pillars, sunnah, manners, and protection from sins that void it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r7.anchor: معنى دوامهم عليها أن يواظبوا على أدائها لا يخلون بها ولا يشتغلون عنها بشيء من الشواغل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r8.claim: The Prophet says the best work is that done most consistently, even when little.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r9.speaker: عائشة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p614/r9.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's practice was continuous and regular.

SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r1.claim: Halu‘an is a prospective circumstantial; the following verses explain the quality through a person’s reaction to harm and good.
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r1.anchor: هلوعا }: حال مقدرة. والهلع مفسر بما بعده، وهو قوله: " إذا " و " إذا

SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r2.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r2.claim: Tha‘lab explains the term from the verse itself: a person shows intense distress at harm and hoards good instead of sharing it.
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r2.anchor: قال ثعلب: " سألني محمد بن عبد الله ابن طاهر ما الهلع؟ فقلت: قد فسره الله

SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd gives the basic lexical sense as the strongest greed and the worst distress.
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r3.anchor: وأصله في اللغة على ما قال أبو عبيد أشد الحرص وأسوأ الجزع

SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r4.claim: Another explanation describes rapid panic and agitation when harm touches someone, and quick refusal when good reaches them; the comparison is a swift-moving she-camel.
SAMIN-DURR:70:19/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو الفزع والاضطراب السريع عند مس المكروه، والمنع السريع عند مس الخير

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r1.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r1.claim: الإنسان in this passage means the disbeliever.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r6.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r6.claim: هلوع means intensely prone to anguish.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r6.anchor: الخامس : أنه الشديد الجزع , قاله مجاهد .

MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan defines the human as impatient in hardship and withholding in prosperity, saying this is how humanity was created.
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.anchor: سألت الحسن عن قوله عز وجل ﴿ خلق هلوعا ﴾ قال اقرأ ما بعدها فقرأت ﴿ إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.claim: “The human” denotes the species, allowing worshippers to be excepted; Ibn ʿAbbās explains halūʿ by the next two verses as quickly distressed at harm and withholding at good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تفسيره ما بعده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.claim: Halūʿ is quick distress when touched by harm and quick withholding when touched by good; one who receives good hoards it and denies it to others.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.anchor: والهلع سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه لسرعة المنع عند مس الخير

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.speaker: محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.claim: When asked by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir, Thaʿlab replied that God's own explanation is clearest.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.anchor: وسأل محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر ثعلبا عن الهلع فقال قد فسره الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.claim: This is human temperament, but people are commanded to oppose their temperament and follow revealed law; harm may be poverty or illness and good may be wealth or health.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.anchor: وهذا طبعه وهو مأمور بمخالفة طبعه وموافقة شرعه والشر الضر والفقر والخير السعة

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r1.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the human created as halu‘ as a disbeliever.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r2.claim: Halu‘ linguistically means extreme greed and the worst, most excessive panic; the intensified form describes a person impatient in good and hardship.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r3.claim: Ikrima defines halu‘ as fretful and distressed.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r3.anchor: عكرمة: هو الضجور. الضحاك: هو الذي لا يشبع

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the halu‘ person is never satiated.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r5.claim: The miserly person is one who receives wealth but withholds God’s due from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r5.anchor: هو الذي إذا أصاب المال منع منه حق الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysan says people love what pleases them and flee what displeases them, yet God commands them to spend what they love and endure what they dislike.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r6.anchor: ثم تعبده الله بإنفاق ما يحب والصبر على ما يكره

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda, as transmitted by Tha‘lab, defines halu‘ as failing to give thanks when blessed and failing to endure harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r7.anchor: هو الذي إذا مسه الخير لم يشكر، وإذا مسه الضر لم يصبر، قاله ثعلب

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r8.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r8.claim: Tha‘lab also reads the following verses as defining halu‘: extreme distress when harmed and withholding good from people when prosperous.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r8.anchor: إذا ناله الشر أظهر شدة الجزع، وإذا ناله الخير بخل به ومنعه الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r9.claim: A prophetic saying calls grasping greed and destabilizing cowardice the worst gifts given to a servant.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r9.anchor: شر ما أعطي العبد شح هالع وجبن خالع

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r10.claim: Arab usage also calls a fast-moving, light-footed she-camel halwa‘a or halwa‘; a cited line witnesses to that word.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r10.anchor: ناقة هلواعة وهلواع إذا كانت سريعة السير خفيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r11.claim: “Jazu‘an” and “manu‘an” are adjectives for halu‘, understood as moved forward before the following conditional, or as the predicate of an implied kana.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:19/r11.anchor: نعتان لهلوع. على أن ينوي بهما التقديم قبل

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.claim: The passage echoes 41:49–51, where people persist in asking for good, despair when harmed, and withdraw after receiving mercy.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.anchor: The message in these verses is similar to that of 41:49–51

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r2.claim: The verse also recalls descriptions of humanity as hasty in 21:37 and 17:11.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r2.anchor: This verse is similar to 21:37, Man was created of haste, and 17:11

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r3.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r3.claim: Here and in the parallel verses, man may mean humanity generally or disbelievers in particular.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r3.anchor: according to some, disbelievers in particular (Q, Ṭ).19

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.claim: Because the passage exempts those who pray, it suggests that the traits describe humanity broadly.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.anchor: the exception save those who perform prayer (v. 22) suggests that the broader interpretation is intended

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r5.claim: Hulūʿ combines greed and covetousness with severe anxiety.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r5.anchor: hulūʿ, which denotes greed and covetousness combined with severe anxiety

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r8.claim: To overcome anxiety, recognize that circumstances come from God and be content with them.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r8.anchor: one should realize that the circumstances that give rise to them are from God and be content with them

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī says health and wealth should be spent to seek gain in the Hereafter rather than this life.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.anchor: they should be expended for the sake of seeking gain in the Hereafter rather than gain in this life

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.claim: Those who possess the eight qualities in 70:22–35 are exempt from the blameworthy state described here.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.anchor: Those characterized by the eight qualities mentioned in the following verses (vv. 22–35) are then not subject to the blameworthy state

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.claim: The human described is the disbeliever, created with intense anxiety: extreme panic combined with greed, impatience, and frustration.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: إن الإنسان الكافر خلق هلوعا والهلع: شدة الجزع مع شدة الحرص والضجر

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person as the one who panics when harmed and withholds when given good, and says this describes associators.

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses halūʿ as miserly and panic-stricken.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r3.anchor: عن جعفر بن أبي المغيرة، عن سعيد بن جبير، {إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا} [المعارج: 19] قال: شحيحا جزوعا

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r4.claim: ʿIkrima defines halūʿ as fretful or easily vexed.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، {إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا} [المعارج: 19] قال: ضجورا

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the disbeliever is stingy and withholds good, panicking when misfortune strikes.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.anchor: هو بخيل منوع للخير، جزوع إذا نزل به البلاء

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r6.speaker: حصين
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r6.claim: Ḥuṣayn glosses halūʿ as greedy or covetous.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r6.anchor: سألت حصينا عن هذه الآية: {إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا}

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses halūʿ as panic-stricken.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r7.anchor: في قوله: {إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا} [المعارج: 19] قال: الهلوع: الجزوع

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r8.claim: Qatāda likewise says halūʿ means panic-stricken.

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r1.claim: The verses identify innate panic as the root that can drive people to turn away and hoard, leading to Hell; it was created to guide people toward their good, but misuse can ruin them.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r1.anchor: السبب الأولي الذي يدعو الإنسان إلى رذيلة الإدبار والتولي والجمع والإيعاء

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.claim: Haluʿ means intense eagerness; the following verses aptly explain it as panic at harm and withholding when good comes.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.anchor: الهلوع صفة مشتقة من الهلع بفتحتين وهو شدة الحرص

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.claim: Human eagerness targets what a person sees as good or useful for himself, producing distress at harm and selfish withholding of benefits.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.anchor: بل حرصا منه على ما يراه خيرا لنفسه أو نافعا في سبيل الخير

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.claim: Innate eagerness rooted in self-love is not itself a vice; it enables pursuit of happiness and becomes blameworthy only through excess, deficiency, or poor judgment.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.anchor: وهي الوسيلة الوحيدة التي تدعو الانسان إلى بلوغ سعادته وكمال وجوده

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.claim: Children initially pursue whatever their instincts present as good and resist sharing; reason later revises their judgments, while persistent appetite can lead to rejecting truth and violating others' rights.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.anchor: فإن أقام على ما كان عليه من اتباع أهواء النفس والعكوف على المشتهيات

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.claim: As reason develops, eagerness can turn toward real good: fear of sin and haste toward forgiveness, while worldly hardship and duty call for the patience God prescribes.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.anchor: إذا رزق البلوغ والرشد زاد تجهيزا آخر وهو العقل الذي بها يدرك حقائق الأمور

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.claim: When people ignore reason and follow appetite without limits, they turn a God-given means of happiness into a cause of misery, withdrawal, and hoarding.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.anchor: فقد بدل نعمة الله نقمة وأخذ صفة غريزية خلقها الله وسيلة له

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r3.claim: There is no contradiction in saying people are created with haluʿ while condemning it: the blame concerns human misuse, as with other created blessings.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r3.anchor: لا ضير في نسبة هلع الإنسان في الآيات إلى الخلقة والكلام مسوق للذم

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari avoids attributing a blameworthy act to God by treating the wording as a metaphor: people favor panic and withholding so strongly that they seem innately stamped with them.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r4.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري فرارا من الإشكال أن في الكلام استعارة

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues the believers' exception shows the trait is not literally created in everyone.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r5.anchor: ومن الدليل عليه استثناء المؤمنين الذين جاهدوا أنفسهم فنجوا عن الجزع والمنع جميعا

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r6.claim: The author rejects the metaphorical escape: the trait is a created blessing, while blame falls on people who mismanage it; believers preserve its good form rather than lack it.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r6.anchor: واستثناء المؤمنين ليس لأجل أن الصفة غير مخلوقة فيهم بل لأجل أنهم أبقوها على كمالها

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites believers who struggle against themselves and escape panic and withholding as evidence for his metaphorical reading.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r7.anchor: ومن الدليل عليه استثناء المؤمنين الذين جاهدوا أنفسهم فنجوا عن الجزع والمنع جميعا

THALABI:v10p38/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r18.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p38/r18.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses haluʿ as miserly.

THALABI:v10p38/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r19.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p38/r19.claim: Ikrima glosses haluʿ as fretful or impatient.

THALABI:v10p38/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r20.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
THALABI:v10p38/r20.claim: Al-Dahhak and Hasan interpret haluʿ as stingy.

THALABI:v10p38/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r22.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
THALABI:v10p38/r22.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd say the person is sorrowful or grief-stricken.

THALABI:v10p38/r24.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r24.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p38/r24.claim: Al-Dahhak also says haluʿ describes someone who is never satisfied.
THALABI:v10p38/r24.anchor: وعن الضحاك أيضا: الهلوع الذي لا يشبع

THALABI:v10p38/r26.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r26.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p38/r26.claim: Ibn Kaysan describes a person who loves what pleases him, flees what displeases him, yet is commanded to give what he loves and endure what he dislikes.
THALABI:v10p38/r26.anchor: ابن كيسان: خلق الله الإنسان يحب ما يسره ويرضيه ويهرب مما يكرهه ويسخطه

THALABI:v10p38/r27.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p38/r27.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p38/r27.claim: Ata glosses haluʿ as hasty; the excerpt starts another gloss without preserving its wording.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r11.claim: The lexicon explains هلوع as intense greed and little patience, with forms from the root ه ل ع illustrated by hunger and distress.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r11.anchor: يقال: هلع الرجل، يهلع هلعا وهلاعا، فهو هالع وهلوع، وهو شدة الحرص، وقلة الصبر، يقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r12.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r12.claim: Amr ibn Maʿdikarib's line is cited as poetic evidence for the word هلع.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r12.anchor: قال عمرو بن معديكرب: ما إن جزعت ولا هلع ... ت ولا يرد بكاي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r13.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r13.claim: Al-Farra defines هلوع as irritable or fretful.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r14.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r14.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats panic and impatience as one sense and invokes seeking God's protection from panic in battle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p221/r14.anchor: وقال المبرد: الهلع، والجزع: يقال (¬8): نعوذ بالله من الهلع عند # منازلة الأقران

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r9.claim: Halūʿ expresses a vague bad temperament between haste, impatience, whining, intensity, and greed; the next verses explain it.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r9.anchor: “Helû‘”, esasında bir çabukluk mânası bulunan bir taraftan tahammülsüzlük, mızıkçılık

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r1.claim: Halūʿ means impatient and intensely desirous, encompassing natural failings such as greed, dissatisfaction, haste, restlessness, despair, and complaint.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r1.anchor: helû‘ kelimesi sözlükte “sabırsız ve bir şeye aşırı derecede düşkün” anlamlarına gelen bir sıfat olup tamahkârlık, tatminsizlik, acelecilik, sabırsızlık, tahammülsüzlük, yılgınlık ve sızlanma

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.claim: The generic definite al-nafs parallels generic human statements qualified by exceptions; the verse forbids killing any protected life, Muslim or treaty-holder, except for a legally valid cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية نهي عن قتل النفس المحرمة، مؤمنة كانت أو معاهدة إلا بالحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r3.claim: Halaʿ is rapid fear and agitation at hardship and rapid withholding when good arrives; the name is linked to a swift-moving she-camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r3.anchor: الهلع: الفزع والاضطراب السريع عند مسن المكروه، والمنع السريع عند مس الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda defines halaʿ as the greatest greed and the worst anxiety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الهلع في اللغة أشد الحرص وأسوأ الجزع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r5.claim: Jazaʿ means fear; a cited poetic line demonstrates the word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p269/r5.anchor: الجزع: الخوف، قال الشاعر: جزعت ولم أجزع من البين مجزعا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr, citing al-Ṣiḥāḥ, glosses halūʿ as extreme greed and the worst, most excessive panic; calamity yields much panic and prosperity yields much withholding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "قال في الصحاح: الهلع في اللغة: أَشَدُّ الحرص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p162/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p162/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p162/r1.claim: The traits surrounding the protection of chastity are a remedy for haluʿ: resisting desire trains a person to be patient instead of rushing after every tempting opportunity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p162/r1.anchor: هذه الآيات مرتبطةٌ بما قبلها أجمل ارتباط. وهي مع ما ذُكِرَ معها من الأوصاف مَنْجاةٌ من الهلع وعلاج له.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.claim: The author observes that the descriptions in al-Muʾminūn and al-Maʿārij are strongly parallel but also differ in wording and order.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.anchor: هناك تشابه كبير بين النصين، كما أن هناك اختلافاً بينهما كما هو ظاهر:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r1.claim: Persistent prayer treats panic by cultivating continuous patience; people often pray but fail to maintain attention because their thoughts and distractions take much of the prayer away.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r1.anchor: فالدوام عليها علاج من أنجع الأدوية للتعويد على الصبر والمعافاة من الجزع.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.claim: Persistent prayer also treats withholding: a worshipper gives God the self and time, and learns freedom from desires even when worship brings no obvious worldly gain or costs an immediate opportunity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.anchor: ذلك أن الدائم في صلاته يتعود أن يُعطي من نفسه ووقته لربه، بل يعطيه نَفْسَهُ كُلَّها ووقته في الصلاة،

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r1.claim: Because humans cannot independently accomplish all their needs, they must communicate their thoughts to others; among several means, spoken words are easiest and best.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r1.anchor: الإنسان خلق بحيث لا يستقل بتحصيل جميع مهماته فاحتاج إلى أن يعرف غيره ما في ضميره

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r2.claim: Speech is easier than writing or gesture because breath and its articulations produce sounds and letters naturally, without comparable effort or assistance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r2.anchor: هذه المعاني تحصل من غير كلفة ومعونة بخلاف الكتابة والإشارة وغيرهما

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r3.claim: Sounds appear when needed and quickly disappear when the need ends, making speech well suited to communication.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r3.anchor: هذه الأصوات كما توجد تفنى عقيبه في الحال فعند الاحتياج إليه تحصل وعند زوال الحاجة تفنى وتنقضي

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r4.claim: Many articulations yield many letters, whose combinations generate almost limitless words, allowing meanings to be distinguished without the confusion found in gesture or clapping.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r4.anchor: تلك الحروف الكثيرة بحسب تركيباتها الكثيرة يتولد منها كلمات تكاد أن تصير غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r5.claim: Human perfection is knowing truth for its own sake and knowing the good in order to act; the soul begins without these perfections and needs the body to acquire them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r5.anchor: كمال الإنسان في أن يعرف الحق لذاته والخير لأجل العمل به وجوهر النفس في أصل الخلقة عار

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r6.claim: The body is created to serve the soul's acquisition of knowledge and action, while the heart supplies the body's innate heat.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r6.anchor: فصار تخليق هذا البدن مطلوبا لهذه الحكمة ثم إن مصالح هذا البدن ما كانت تتم إلا إذا كان القلب ينبوعا للحرارة الغريزية

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r7.claim: Because innate heat is strong, the heart must ventilate itself: expansion draws in cool air, which warms, then contraction expels it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r7.anchor: جعل للقلب قوة انبساط بها يجذب الهواء البارد من خارج البدن إلى نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r8.claim: Razi explains animal breathing as the heart's expansion drawing air inward and contraction squeezing warmed air outward.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r8.anchor: انعصر ما فيه من الهواء وخرج إلى الخارج

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r9.claim: The hierarchy of purposes runs from perfecting the soul, to creating the body and heart, to enabling expansion and contraction, and then directing expelled air toward sound.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r9.anchor: والمقصود بالقصد الأول هو تكميل جوهر النفس بالعلم والعمل فوقع تخليق البدن في المرتبة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r10.claim: At the next level, expelled air becomes sound's material; the Creator gives the throat, tongue, teeth, and lips articulating stops that produce distinct letters and words.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r10.anchor: جعل هذا الأمر المطلوب على سبيل الغرض الواقع في المرتبة السابعة مادة للصوت وخلق محابس ومقاطع للصوت في الحلق واللسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r11.claim: Articulated sounds form many different letters, whose combinations produce words without end.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r11.anchor: وحينئذ يحدث بذلك السبب هذه الحروف المختلفة ويحدث من تركيباتها الكلمات التي لا نهاية لها

RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r12.claim: Speech carries profound wisdom and secrets beyond the grasp of earlier and later minds, prompting praise of the wise Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v1p32/r12.anchor: ثم أودع في هذا النطق والكلام حكما عالية وأسرارا باهرة عجزت عقول الأولين والآخرين عن الإحاطة

BURHAN:v3p36/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.claim: The clauses describing the human as anxious when harmed and withholding when prosperous explain هلوعا; explanatory clauses are common in the Qur’an.
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p36/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī says one should not stop before an explanatory clause, because it completes the explanation much like a relative clause or adjective completes its noun.
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جنى ومتى كانت الجملة تفسيرا لم يحسن الوقف على ما قبلها دونها

ITQAN:v2p386#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p386#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p386#2/r4.anchor: 2575 ﴿ صغت ﴾ مالت 2576 ﴿ هلوعا ﴾ ضجورا 2577 ﴿ شططا ﴾ كذبا

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.speaker: أهل البيان
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.claim: The people of rhetoric describe an explanatory clause as something added to remove ambiguity and clarify what came before it.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.anchor: قال أهل البيان وهو أن يكون في الكلام لبس وخفاء فيؤتى بما يزيله ويفسره

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية وغيره
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya and others take the clauses about his reaction to harm and good as an explanation of هلوعا.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.anchor: فقوله ( إذا مسه ) الخ تفسير للهلوع كما قال أبو العالية وغيره

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jinni says one should not pause before an explanatory sentence because it completes and functions as part of what it explains.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن جني ومتى كانت الجملة تفسيرا لم يحسن الوقف على ما قبلها دونها لأن تفسير الشيء لا حق به ومتمم له وجار مجرى بعض أجزائه
